statement: Release sets conns, factory, ping and close to nil and does not modify connReqs.
The only place that returns ErrMaxActiveConnReached is the branch where the waiter channel is closed, and no statement in the file closes a waiter channel.
Close decrements openingConns without signalling or removing any waiter in connReqs.
When conns is nil, Put returns the result of Close(conn).
When the close callback is nil, Close returns nil without decrementing openingConns and without closing the connection.
Ping calls c.ping without checking whether it is nil and without taking the mutex.
Get calls the factory while holding the mutex.
Close calls the close callback while holding the mutex.
When a Get receives a connection from its waiter channel, it checks the idle timeout but does not call Ping.
In Get, the select that tests for an idle connection runs before the mutex is acquired in the default branch.
The waitTimeOut field is declared but never assigned or read.
Put removes the first waiter from connReqs before sending the connection to it.
Release closes only the connections buffered in the conns channel, after releasing the mutex.
Get returns ErrClosed when its snapshot of conns is nil.
Len returns the number of connections buffered in the conns channel snapshot.
When Get discards an expired idle connection it ignores the error returned by Close.
NewChannelPool sets openingConns to InitialCap before it creates the initial connections.
The capacity validation accepts InitialCap = 0, MaxIdle = 0 and MaxCap = 0.
A second Release returns early because its snapshot of conns is nil.
Put gives a handed-off connection a new timestamp of the current time.
Put does not check whether the connection is already in the pool before enqueueing it.
After discarding an expired idle connection Get continues its loop with no bound on the number of iterations.
